Indices of residential segregation

Source: R/dissix.R
dissix.Rd

The evenness of groups across areal units (Massey and Denton 1988), from a table of counts with one row per unit and one column per group: Duncan's dissimilarity D = sum |x_ik / X_k - x_il / X_l| / 2 between each pair of groups (the share of either group that would have to move for the two to be spread alike), and for each group against the rest the segregation index IS, Theil's entropy index H, Atkinson's index with shape delta and the Gini index. With weights w between the units, Morrill's (1991) adjusted D subtracts the weighted mean absolute difference of the pair's shares between neighbouring units, so that segregation across a boundary counts less than segregation within. Units with no one in them are left out. That D lies between 0 and 1 is proved in Lean: see proof("dissix").

Usage

dissix(x, delta = 0.5, w = NULL)

Arguments

x

The counts: a matrix or data frame of numbers from 0, units by groups (named columns), every group with a positive total.

delta

Atkinson's shape, above 0 and below 1.

w

NULL, or weights between the units (as gmoran() takes them), with a positive total.

Value

A list of class dissix: d, the matrix of D; grp, a data frame of group, is, h, atk and gini; dm, NULL or the matrix of Morrill's D; and delta.

References

Duncan, O. D. and Duncan, B. (1955). A methodological analysis of segregation indexes. American Sociological Review, 20(2), 210-217. doi:10.2307/2088328

Massey, D. S. and Denton, N. A. (1988). The dimensions of residential segregation. Social Forces, 67(2), 281-315. doi:10.2307/2579183

Morrill, R. L. (1991). On the measure of geographic segregation. Geography Research Forum, 11, 25-36.

Examples

x <- cbind(a = c(90, 80, 10, 5, 50), b = c(10, 20, 85, 95, 50))
dissix(x)
#> dissix: dissimilarity between groups
#>           a         b
#> a 0.0000000 0.6284779
#> b 0.6284779 0.0000000
#>  group        is         h       atk      gini
#>      a 0.6284779 0.4052672 0.5217079 0.7680033
#>      b 0.6284779 0.4052672 0.5217079 0.7680033
dissix(x, w = spwt(nb = list(2, c(1, 3), c(2, 4), c(3, 5), 4),
                   type = "contig"))$dm
#>           a         b
#> a 0.0000000 0.3134779
#> b 0.3134779 0.0000000
